# Known issues in 1.0.1

Please report bugs: this is a big game, and some parts have been tested only in an emulator.

## Fixed in 1.0.1

- Menus close with the B button again, as in Pearl: the Trainers' School blackboard, the shops' floor lists, elevators and more. The blackboard opens its list of lessons, so you can leave it.
- No more hangs after the Jubilife TV boards, the Move Deleter and other places that opened nothing. The Move Deleter in Canalave City deletes moves.
- The Oreburgh Mining Museum restores fossils, and the in-game trades happen: Oreburgh City, Eterna City, Snowpoint City and Route 226.
- Barry's name shows on the Canalave bridge when you talk to him after the battle. The Old Chateau's ghosts appear sometimes, as in the original.
- Pokémon shown in a scene (Mesprit, Cresselia, the Celestic elder's picture) are marked seen in the Pokédex, and Mesprit and Cresselia start roaming right after their scenes.
- Eggs count as Eggs again: the Move Deleter, the Day Care and Grandma Wilma say so. Pastoria City's Burmy boy checks your party for all three cloaks before he gives the Macho Brace.
- Deoxys changes form at Veilstone's meteorites. Floaroma Town's flower shop trades Accessories for Berries.
- The ribbon givers give ribbons: Dr. Footstep on Route 213, Julia and the Sunyshore Market in Sunyshore City, the Ribbon Syndicate in the Resort Area, which checks your money right for its 100,000 and 999,999 ribbons. The scarf man in Pastoria City gives scarves ([Super Contests](super-contests.md)).
- The Game Corner's prize TMs are sold at the Veilstone Department Store, 3F, and its Silk Scarf, Wide Lens, Zoom Lens and Metronome at 2F. Its coin clerk gives TM64, and the Battle Point Exchange's TM59 is Dragon Pulse ([TMs and HMs](tms-and-hms.md)).
- All 25 Pokétch apps can be obtained, and the developer in Sunyshore checks your party for the nature he names ([the Pokétch](poketch.md)).
- Mr. Goods in Hearthome gives his cups and Crystals, and the Battle Tower its trophies: its attendant appears when one is waiting for you ([Secret Bases](secret-bases.md#mr-goods-and-the-battle-tower)). The Tower lobby's results machines show your win streaks, and its leaders machine says it has no data yet: reading one no longer stops the game.
- A new game goes from Professor Rowan's talk straight to your bedroom, with no glimpse of Twinleaf Town in between.
- Adamant Diamond: Pal Park's slate clerk trades for all of Diamond's slates, so the Johto Room and the rooms after it open (1.0's clerk offered Pearl's).
- Wayward Cave's entrance under the Cycling Road takes you in (walking into it only bumped the rock), and you come back out on the ground under the bridge.
- People and the player stand at the right height: Azelf and Uxie can be reached and Verity Cavern's pool can be walked round; on the lakes and at Sendoff Spring you surf on the water, not under it; the Elite Four's doors close in their doorways and Cynthia's room leads to the Hall of Fame; people stand on the floor in the Veilstone Game Corner and the Battle Tower, and you arrive on the floor at the Pal Park gate. No more invisible steps, bumps or drops in Pokémon Center 2F, the Canalave Gym, on the Contest Hall's stage stairs, Iron Island's lifts and at the Great Marsh's edges. Pal Park's Rainbow Room doorway no longer lifts you onto the cliff top.
- Celestic Town's south edge shows the mountain top, not a black band. Far fewer thin black lines between map pieces, such as Route 211's cliff by the water, Valor Lakefront's cliff, Route 210 North and the Contest Hall lobby's back wall.
- The Pokédex's AREA page shows the honey trees, the Great Marsh and Feebas. Adamant Diamond has its own Pokédex entries, and in Lustrous Pearl the other forms of Rotom, Giratina, Shaymin and Arceus show Pearl's entry instead of Black 2's.
- After the Hall of Fame every Pokémon can be caught in either version: the other version's, Mew, Celebi, Jirachi, Deoxys and the Poké Radar's. See the post-game pages: [Lustrous Pearl](postgame-pearl.md#the-whole-national-pokédex), [Adamant Diamond](postgame-diamond.md#the-whole-national-pokédex).

## Super Contests

- Hearts, Voltage and result bars are numbers rather than the original pictures. The judges aren't on stage.
- During Visual, the top screen shows numbers instead of your dressed Pokémon.
- The curtain doesn't count in Visual's score, and the backdrop stays the first one.
- Black 2's sounds stand in for the contests' and the Digger Drill's.

## Poffins

- Cooking is solo, with simplified art: the pot's rim and ring don't turn (the batter does), the overflow and burn puffs and the DONE! banner are lines of text instead.

## Secret Bases

- No Radar and no other players' bases. A placed good can wall you in, as in the original: Move Goods frees you.
- Mr. Goods' Globe needs Wi-Fi, so it isn't given.

## Not in this version

- Digging in the Underground (treasures, Spheres, traps). See [the Underground page](underground.md) for how treasures come instead.
- Online features, and the Battle Tower's Wi-Fi and wireless rooms.
- **The Veilstone Game Corner and its Prize Exchange are closed.** Its prizes are sold at the Veilstone Department Store: the TMs at 3F (see [TMs and HMs](tms-and-hms.md)), Silk Scarf, Wide Lens, Zoom Lens and Metronome at 2F.
- The Game Boy Advance migration at Pal Park is in the build but unconfirmed: see [Pal Park](ramanas-park-pearl.md#bringing-pokémon-from-a-game-boy-advance-game).
- The Great Marsh's Quick Tram and binoculars, and its Safari rules: you walk, with a $500 fee and 30 Safari Balls, and normal battles.
- No Poké Radar (Professor Oak still hands you one; the Pokémon only it found come after the Hall of Fame), no Game Boy Advance-slot Pokémon in wild grass, no Seals or Ball Capsules (the Seal Case is given; Sunyshore's Seal clerk has no stock).

## People who talk but can't do their job yet

- The Loto at Jubilife TV, and the Global Trade Station.
- The Route 222 size contest, and the Vista Lighthouse binoculars.

## Small things

- Route 224's stone tablet doesn't keep your inscription; read later, it names you.
- The Pokémon World Tournament's lobby still mentions Unova in places.
- Honey trees don't shake, and Berry patches don't sway.
